properties.description:
TORILM

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
West Central Columbus County in southeastern North Carolina...
Southern Robeson County in southeastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Dillon County in northeastern South Carolina...
Northwestern Horry County in northeastern South Carolina...
Northeastern Marion County in northeastern South Carolina...

* Until 1130 AM EDT.

* At 1100 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located over Mullins, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Mullins, Fair Bluff, Lake View, Kemper, Fork, Cherry Grove, Gapway,
Smithboro, Zion, Nichols, Cerro Gordo and Carolinas Hospital System
- Marion.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Please send your reports of hail or wind damage by calling the
National Weather Service office in Wilmington at 1 800 697 3901.

feet on 02/13/2018.

properties.instruction:

properties.areaDesc: Alexander, NC; Catawba, NC; Iredell, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 10:33AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Alexander County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...
North Central Catawba County in the piedmont of North Carolina...
West Central Iredell County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...River flows and lake levels are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1021 AM EDT, After a 4 to 7 inch rain event in the headwaters
of the Catawba River, runoff has resulted in high flows and lake
pool elevations.  The Lookout Shoals Lake level will continue to
rise today possibly causing flooding of shorelines, lake access
areas, campgrounds, docks and residential yards. Caution is
advised in these areas.
- Residents are encouraged to heed guidance from local officials
and Emergency Management on any potential impacts to property.
In addition, please contact Catawba County Emergency Management
to update their contact information using the following link to
their Community Alert system web page at:
www.catawbacountync.gov/online-services/community- alert-system/

For more information on lake levels or dam releases, please visit
http://lakes.duke-energy.com or call 1-800-829-5253.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding threatening
roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.
